data.name: TraySelectDeviceText
data.value: Open “Settings” from the tray icon menu and check a device.

data.name: TrayReconnectTooltip
data.value: The device is connected to this computer. Click to disconnect and connect it again.

data.name: AppleDriverInfo
data.value: Apple’s Boot Camp driver adds the Fn key (Fn+Backspace = Delete, media keys) to Magic Keyboard 2015–2021. It is downloaded from Apple’s servers when you install it.

data.name: AppleDriverInstalling
data.value: Installing (confirm the administrator prompt if asked)…

data.name: AppleDriverInstallDone
data.value: Driver installed. Reconnect the keyboard to apply.

data.name: AppleDriverInstallReboot
data.value: Driver installed. Restart Windows to apply.

data.name: AppleDriverUpToDate
data.value: The driver is already installed and up to date.

data.name: AppleDriverInstallNoDevice
data.value: Driver added, but no connected keyboard uses it yet. Connect the Magic Keyboard and reconnect it.

data.name: AppleFnAppliedNow
data.value: Applied. Fn+Esc switches it at any time.

data.name: AppleFnApplied
data.value: Applied. Fn+Esc switches it at any time.

data.name: TrayConnectTooltip
data.value: Connect the device to this computer

data.name: ResultNotFound
data.value: “{0}” was not found among paired devices.

data.name: ResultAccessDenied
data.value: Windows did not allow reinstalling the device services without administrator rights. Choose “Restart as administrator” in the menu.

data.name: ResultNoRadio
data.value: Bluetooth adapter not found or turned off.

data.name: ResultBleAlreadyConnected
data.value: “{0}” (BLE) is already connected. Windows does not support forcing a BLE reconnect.

data.name: ResultNotConnected
data.value: “{0}” did not respond. Make sure the device is turned on and nearby. Some devices accept incoming connections only on the active channel.

data.name: SettingsHint
data.value: Check the devices (keyboards, speakers, headphones…) to show in the tray menu. Clicking a menu item connects the device; if it is already connected, it is disconnected and connected again. The device must be paired with this computer beforehand.

data.name: SettingsNoneFound
data.value: No paired devices found. Pair a device in Windows Settings.

data.name: SettingsFoundCount
data.value: Devices found: {0}. Select a device to configure its services.

data.name: ServicesGroupBle
data.value: Services to reconnect: {0} — not applicable to BLE

data.name: ServicesGroupNotFound
data.value: Services to reconnect: {0} — device not found

data.name: ServicesAuto
data.value: Automatic (keyboard/mouse — HID, speaker/headphones — all audio profiles)

data.name: ServicesNote
data.value: Each service takes about 3 s to reconnect. For a speaker or headset, all audio profiles are reconnected: the microphone (Hands-Free) often comes back only after a full reconnect. After reconnecting, the app checks that the microphone is there.

data.name: SettingsAutoStartFailed
data.value: Could not change the startup settings: {0}

data.name: ResultPullFailed
data.value: “{0}” did not connect. Turn the keyboard off and on (or press a key) and try again.

data.name: ServiceInfo
data.value: The Windows service restores the devices marked “Restore at startup and sign-in”, even before you sign in, and performs actions that need administrator rights, so the app itself runs without them. It is installed to Program Files (one administrator confirmation).

data.name: ServiceRunningOutdated
data.value: Running an older version ({0}): update it

data.name: RestoreAtStartupNote
data.value: Also on the Windows sign-in screen. If another device took it over, it is paired again without a dialog. Needs the background service.

data.name: ResultNoMicrophone
data.value: “{0}” is connected, but its microphone did not come back. Try again, or turn the device off and on.

data.name: TrayRestartAudioTooltip
data.value: When sound or the microphone stops working: restarts the Windows audio services and the Bluetooth audio of the audio processor (Intel Smart Sound), then reconnects the selected speakers and headsets.

data.name: AudioRestartedReconnecting
data.value: Windows audio has been restarted. Reconnecting the speakers and headsets…

data.name: AppleFnSignInNote
data.value: Fn+Esc switches the top row between F-keys and media keys at any time. In the F-keys mode F3–F12 work without Fn; F1 and F2 always need Fn (Apple’s driver keeps the brightness keys to itself). On the sign-in and lock screens the top row sends media keys.

data.name: RemapTitle
data.value: Remap keys of the Apple keyboard

data.name: RemapNote
data.value: Applies to Apple keyboards only (Bluetooth and USB); other keyboards are not affected. With the background service it works in all windows, including those run as administrator; without it, not in administrator windows. It does not work on the sign-in and lock screens. Changes apply when you save the settings.

data.name: KeyboardHint
data.value: The keyboard gets a “Connect” item in the tray menu: it brings the keyboard to this computer after another device used it. Double-click the tray icon does the same when it is the only device in the menu.

data.name: ExperimentalNote
data.value: Experimental: one-click reconnect for other Bluetooth devices — speakers, headphones, other keyboards and mice. It depends on the device and does not work with every one.

data.name: SettingsWatchMicrophone
data.value: Notify when a Bluetooth speaker or headset loses its microphone

data.name: SettingsRestoreMicrophoneNote
data.value: Restarts Windows audio: sound in all apps is interrupted for a few seconds, also during a call. Needs the background service; without it you get the notification.

data.name: MicrophoneLostText
data.value: “{0}” is connected without its microphone. Click here, or choose “Restore the microphone” in the tray menu, to bring it back (sound is interrupted for a few seconds).

data.name: MicrophoneLostFixing
data.value: “{0}” lost its microphone. Restarting Windows audio to bring it back…
